title: Food insecurity is a graded household-security outcome with family shielding and institutional coping
source_unit: USDA Food Security Supplement household, child-household, poverty, and assistance measures

observations.method: USDA ERS 2024 Food Security Supplement published estimate; this record uses the published percentage base because the committed memo records the rounded percentage and count rather than the full household denominator.
observations.uncertainty: The national rate was not statistically different from 2023; no interval is reproduced here. The measure does not identify a causal price, employer, policy, store, or household event.
observations.counterinterpretation: A prevalence rate is not a purchase diary, price trend, or proof that households had the same experience or response.

observations.period: 2024; severity distribution among all US households
observations.method: USDA ERS 2024 Food Security Supplement severity categories; low and very low food security are retained as distinct outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: No interval is reproduced here. Very low food security captures disrupted eating patterns or reduced intake; questionnaire classification and annual recall remain relevant limitations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low food security is not equivalent to very low food security; combining them obscures the difference between dietary coping and disrupted intake.

observations.method: USDA ERS 2024 Food Security Supplement household-with-children tables; conditional family measures are kept separate from the all-household rate.
observations.uncertainty: No interval is reproduced here. Household shielding and respondent reporting mean the measure does not identify each member's full food experience or a causal family decision.
observations.counterinterpretation: Adults can be food insecure while children are protected in some households; family protection is not a uniform parental choice or proof of adequate security.

observations.method: USDA ERS 2024 Food Security Supplement assistance-participation estimate among households experiencing very low food security in the 30 days before interview.
observations.uncertainty: No interval is reproduced here. Participation is measured in the same period and does not establish benefit adequacy, timing, take-up effort, or restoration of food security.
observations.subgroup: Households with very low food security in the prior 30 days.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance participation is an institutional coping/resource measure, not evidence that the program fully restored food security or removed the underlying constraint.

boundary: This is a national descriptive USDA household-security layer. It does not identify a dated price or institutional trigger, detailed purchases, care/time displacement, health outcome, benefit adequacy, trust, political action, or causal effect. Published rounded percentages and counts are retained; where the committed memo did not preserve a full absolute denominator, the denominator is explicitly labeled as a percentage base. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.
